models._description: Report — embed EDI XML in invoice PDF

behavioral_notes.observation: On posting an invoice, for every account.edi.format enabled on the journal (journal.edi_format_ids) whose _get_move_applicability(move) is truthy, the override creates or resets an account.edi.document in state 'to_send' (one per (move, format), enforced by the UNIQUE(edi_format_id, move_id) constraint). It first runs _check_move_configuration and raises UserError on missing data, then immediately processes synchronous formats via _process_documents_no_web_services and triggers the account_edi.ir_cron_edi_network cron for web-service formats. This is the entry point that turns a posted accounting move into pending electronic documents — invisible in metadata.

account.edi.format is a near-empty abstract base (only name/code fields) whose behavioral methods — _get_move_applicability (returns a dict of post/cancel/post_batching/cancel_batching/edi_content callables), _needs_web_services, _is_compatible_with_journal, _check_move_configuration, _prepare_invoice_report — are stubs explicitly marked 'TO OVERRIDE'. Country localization modules (l10n_*) subclass this model to register concrete e-invoice formats (UBL, Factur-X, FatturaPA, etc.); the framework itself ships no format. The format object is therefore a pluggable strategy: the move-to-XML generation, schema choice and acknowledgement parsing all live in the subclasses, not here.

account.edi.document.state drives a per-(move,format) state machine: to_send -> sent (post flow) and to_cancel -> cancelled (cancel flow), with blocking_level info/warning/error gating retries. _prepare_jobs groups documents by (format,state,company,batching-key) into jobs; _process_job calls the format's post/cancel callable, then _postprocess_post_edi_results writes the returned attachment onto attachment_id (the EDI XML attached to the invoice) and flips state to 'sent', or records the error/blocking_level. The _cron_process_documents_web_services cron searches posted moves with documents in to_send/to_cancel and non-error blocking, locks rows (lock_for_update), commits between jobs, and re-triggers itself while jobs remain — this is the asynchronous send/ack loop. A fully-approved cancel even drives the underlying move to button_draft()+button_cancel().

behavioral_notes.element: account.move cancel/draft EDI gating (button_cancel / button_draft / button_cancel_posted_moves)
behavioral_notes.observation: Once an EDI document is 'sent' via a web service, the move can no longer be freely reset: button_draft raises UserError telling the user to use 'Request EDI Cancellation' instead, button_cancel flips sent documents to 'to_cancel' (request) and others straight to 'cancelled', and button_cancel_posted_moves / button_abandon_cancel_posted_moves manage the cancellation-request lifecycle with chatter messages. _is_ready_to_be_sent is overridden to block the customer email until the EDI document leaves 'to_send'. These legal-immutability couplings between e-invoice transmission state and accounting document state are not expressible in metadata.

No frontend assets: 0 JS files, 0 XML templates, 0 OWL components, 0 registry registrations, 0 patches, no asset bundles. The module is pure server-side EDI plumbing; its UI surfaces (cancel/retry buttons, EDI state, error messages) are rendered through inherited account.move views, not through new OWL components.

0 outbound HTTP call sites, no SDK imports, uses_api_keys=False, no endpoints. The base framework defines the web-service hooks (_needs_web_services / _process_documents_web_services) but performs no external calls itself — the actual government/clearance-platform connectivity lives in the localization subclasses.

it_architecture.application: account_edi (Electronic Data Interchange framework for invoices — application component extending account)
information_flows: side-effect: account.move._post -> creates account.edi.document(state=to_send) per applicable journal format, runs synchronous formats, triggers EDI cron

side-effect: account.edi.document._process_documents_web_services -> calls format post/cancel callables, attaches generated EDI XML (attachment_id) to the move, advances state to_send->sent / to_cancel->cancelled
side-effect: account.move.button_cancel/button_cancel_posted_moves -> requests EDI cancellation (to_cancel); a fully-approved cancel drives the move to draft+cancel
control: ir_cron_edi_network cron re-triggers itself while web-service jobs remain (async send/ack loop)
extension point: account.edi.format subclassed by l10n_* localizations to implement concrete e-invoice formats and clearance-platform calls

capabilities: Transmit E-Invoices via Pluggable Formats & Web Services
Attach EDI Documents to Invoices and Outgoing Mail
Enable Country-Specific E-Invoicing Compliance (via l10n_* extensions)
value_streams: E-Invoice Issue: post invoice -> generate EDI document(to_send) -> transmit (sync or via cron web service) -> sent + XML attached
E-Invoice Cancellation: request cancellation (to_cancel) -> web-service ack -> cancelled (and underlying move drafted/cancelled)
policies: UNIQUE(edi_format_id, move_id): at most one EDI document per move per format
Posted invoice with a 'sent' web-service EDI cannot be reset to draft — must go through 'Request EDI Cancellation'
Customer email blocked (_is_ready_to_be_sent) until the EDI document leaves 'to_send'
blocking_level=error halts processing/retry of a document until cleared
EDI cron only processes posted moves with non-error documents and locks rows to prevent double transmission
stakeholders: Accountant / Billing user (posts invoices, triggers EDI)
Customer / Vendor (recipient of the structured e-invoice)
Tax authority / clearance platform (e-invoicing compliance endpoint, via l10n_*)
metrics: edi_error_count (number of EDIs in error per move)

classification.rationale: account_edi is financial-document interchange infrastructure that extends the accounting backbone (depends solely on account); it has no value stream of its own and creates no primary value — it merely encodes and transmits the invoices that primary activities (sale -> customer invoice) already produced. It is a support activity in Porter/APQC terms, mapping to APQC 9.0 Manage Financial Resources, specifically the invoice-processing / e-invoicing-compliance facet of 9.2.x Process accounts receivable (the structured electronic delivery and legal acknowledgement of the account.move customer invoice). The module is a pluggable framework: account.edi.format is an abstract strategy subclassed by country localizations, so account_edi itself is plumbing, not a revenue- or production-bearing process.

standard_capabilities: per-(move,format) electronic document lifecycle: to_send -> sent -> to_cancel -> cancelled
automatic EDI document creation on invoice posting for each format enabled on the journal
synchronous and asynchronous (cron/web-service) transmission flows with batching
pluggable account.edi.format strategy (post/cancel/edi_content/applicability/web-service hooks) for localizations
generated EDI XML attached to the invoice and added to outgoing 'Send & Print' mail
error/blocking-level handling, retry, and EDI cancellation-request workflow
journal-level configuration of compatible / enabled EDI formats
typical_fits: country e-invoicing via l10n_* modules that subclass account.edi.format (UBL, Factur-X, FatturaPA, etc.)
embedding the structured invoice XML into the invoice PDF for hybrid delivery
asynchronous clearance/transmission via the EDI cron without blocking posting
common_gaps: no concrete EDI format ships in the base framework — a localization module is required to do anything
no inbound EDI import/parsing pipeline beyond the report/attachment hooks (vendor-bill capture lives elsewhere)
direct connectivity to specific government clearance platforms (auth, certificates, endpoints) is localization-specific
no dedicated frontend/dashboard — status surfaces only through inherited account.move views
